bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).

- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# FFmpeg

FFmpeg is a collection of libraries and tools to process multimedia content
such as audio, video, subtitles and related metadata.

## Tools

* **ffmpeg** - A command line toolbox to manipulate, convert and stream multimedia content.
* **ffplay** - A minimalistic multimedia player.
* **ffprobe** - A simple analysis tool to inspect multimedia content.
* Additional small tools such as `aviocat`, `ismindex` and `qt-faststart`.

## Documentation

The online documentation is available at:
- Main website: https://ffmpeg.org
- Wiki: https://trac.ffmpeg.org

FFmpeg codebase is mainly LGPL-licensed with optional components licensed under
GPL. Please refer to the LICENSE file for detailed information.

or later (LGPL v2.1+). Read the file `COPYING.LGPLv2.1` for details. Some other
files have MIT/X11/BSD-style licenses. In combination the LGPL v2.1+ applies to
FFmpeg.

Some optional parts of FFmpeg are licensed under the GNU General Public License
version 2 or later (GPL v2+). See the file `COPYING.GPLv2` for details. None of
these parts are used by default, you have to explicitly pass `--enable-gpl` to

- optional x86 optimization in the files

## External libraries

FFmpeg can be combined with a number of external libraries, which sometimes
affect the licensing of binaries resulting from the combination.

### Compatible libraries

The following libraries are under GPL version 2:
- avisynth
- frei0r
- libcdio
- libdavs2
- librubberband
- libvidstab
- libx264
- libx265
- libxavs
- libxavs2
- libxvid

When combining them with FFmpeg, FFmpeg needs to be licensed as GPL as well by
passing `--enable-gpl` to configure.

The following libraries are under LGPL version 3:
- gmp
- libaribb24
- liblensfun

When combining them with FFmpeg, use the configure option `--enable-version3` to
upgrade FFmpeg to the LGPL v3.

The VMAF, mbedTLS, RK MPI, OpenCORE and VisualOn libraries are under the Apache License

version 3 of those licenses. So to combine these libraries with FFmpeg, the
license version needs to be upgraded by passing `--enable-version3` to configure.

The smbclient library is under the GPL v3, to combine it with FFmpeg,
the options `--enable-gpl` and `--enable-version3` have to be passed to
configure to upgrade FFmpeg to the GPL v3.

### Incompatible libraries

There are certain libraries you can combine with FFmpeg whose licenses are not
compatible with the GPL and/or the LGPL. If you wish to enable these
libraries, even in circumstances that their license may be incompatible, pass
`--enable-nonfree` to configure. This will cause the resulting binary to be
unredistributable.

The Fraunhofer FDK AAC and OpenSSL libraries are under licenses which are
incompatible with the GPLv2 and v3. To the best of our knowledge, they are
compatible with the LGPL.

import struct, math, random, os
def wav(path, ch, sr, bps, frames, fmt_tag=None):
    # frames: list of per-frame tuples of ints
    n=len(frames)
    bs=bps//8
    data=bytearray()
    for fr in frames:
        for v in fr:
            if bps==8: data+=struct.pack('<B', v)
            elif bps==16: data+=struct.pack('<h', v)
            elif bps==24: data+=struct.pack('<i', v)[:3]
            elif bps==32: data+=struct.pack('<i', v)
    fmt=struct.pack('<HHIIHH', 1, ch, sr, sr*ch*bs, ch*bs, bps)
    if fmt_tag=='ext':
        fmt=struct.pack('<HHIIHH', 0xFFFE, ch, sr, sr*ch*bs, ch*bs, bps)+struct.pack('<HHI',22,bps,0)+struct.pack('<H',1)+b'\x00\x00\x00\x00\x10\x00\x80\x00\x00\xaa\x00\x38\x9b\x71'

            out[n2]=0.0

def levinson(ac, maxo):

    lpc=[[0.0]*maxo for _ in range(maxo)]
    last=lpc[0]

        for j in range(i): r-=last[j]*a[i-j-1]

from lpcproto import *
def welch2(data):
    n=len(data); out=[0.0]*n; n2=n>>1; c=2.0/(n-1.0)
    if n&1:
        for i in range(n2):
            w=c-i-1.0; w=1.0-w*w; out[i]=data[i]*w; out[n-1-i]=data[n-1-i]*w
        out[n2]=0.0
    else:
        for i in range(n2):
            w=c-n2+i; w=1.0-w*w; out[n2+i]=data[n2+i]*w; out[n2-i-1]=data[n2-i-1]*w
    return out
def autocorr_seq(data, lag):
    pad=[0.0]*40+data; ac=[0.0]*(lag+1)
    for j in range(lag+1):
        s=1.0
        for i in range(j, len(data)): s+=data[i]*pad[40+i-j]
        ac[j]=s
    return ac
def autocorr_c(data, lag):
    # the C version with pairs for the last lag
    pad=[0.0]*40+data; ac=[0.0]*(lag+1); n=len(data)
    j=0
    while j<lag:
        s0=1.0; s1=1.0
        for i in range(j,n):
            s0+=data[i]*pad[40+i-j]; s1+=data[i]*pad[40+i-j-1]
        ac[j]=s0; ac[j+1]=s1; j+=2
    if j==lag:
        s=1.0
        i=j-1
        while i<n:
            a=data[i]*pad[40+i-j]
            b=(pad[40+i+1]*pad[40+i-j+1]) if i+1<n else 0.0
            s+=a+b; i+=2
        ac[j]=s
    return ac

            if i+1<n: l1+=data[i+1]*pad[40+i+1-j]

    return ac

{"command":"cd /workspace && cat > NOTES.md <<'EOF'
# Implementation notes

This tree contains an original, from-scratch reimplementation of the audio
subset of the `ffmpeg` command line tool that the bundled assets exercise
(WAV <-> FLAC round trips).  Everything was derived from black-box
observation of the reference executable: running it on generated inputs and
inspecting the produced files / messages.

## Layout

* `src/main.c`     – command line parsing, stream setup, log output, encode loop
* `src/demux.c`    – input probing; WAV / FLAC / raw PCM demuxing+decoding; `lavfi` `sine` source
* `src/mux.c`      – WAV, FLAC, raw PCM, md5/hash/crc/framecrc/framemd5/null muxers
* `src/flacenc.c`  – FLAC encoder (bit exact with the reference at all compression levels)
* `src/flacdec.c`  – FLAC bitstream decoder
* `src/sine.c`     – table based sine generator (`-f lavfi -i sine=...`)
* `src/crc.c`      – CRC-8/16, Adler-32, CRC-32, MD5, SHA-1/224/256
* `src/log.c`      – av_log like message handling (levels, repeated line folding)
* `src/helptext.c` – static informational texts (`-h`, `-formats`, ...)
* `tools/test_enc.c` – stand-alone encoder test harness used during development

## Observed encoder behaviour that had to be matched

* block size: largest standard FLAC block size <= sample_rate * block_time_ms / 1000
  (27 ms for levels 0-2, 105 ms otherwise, minimum 192)
* analysis window: `w = 1 - (c - i - 1)^2` with `c = 2/(len-1)` for odd lengths
  (centre sample zeroed), `w = 1 - (c - n2 + i)^2` for even lengths
* autocorrelation: two interleaved accumulators (even/odd indices), lane 0
  seeded with 1.0, summed at the end; for odd lengths `data[len]` (zero) is read
* Levinson-Durbin in double precision, coefficient quantisation with `lrintf`
  on the running error, 15 bit precision, shift search from 15 downwards
* order selection: "estimation" method (highest reflection coefficient > 0.1),
  2/4/8 level, log and full search methods for the higher levels
* rice parameter estimate: `k = log2((sum - n/2) / n)`, cost
  `n*(k+1) + ((sum - n/2) >> k)`, 4 bits per partition parameter even in
  RICE2 mode, partition orders searched from the maximum downwards with
  strict "less than" comparison
* stereo decorrelation chosen from second order residual sums, side channel
  gets one extra bit; wasted bit removal stops at the first channel without
  wasted bits
* verbatim fallback when the frame is larger than the maximum frame size;
  the threshold is recomputed when a block is shorter than the previous one
* 24 bit material uses RICE2 (5 bit parameters), s32 input with other than
  24 valid bits prints the "experimental" warning and is encoded as 24 bit
EOF
git add -A && git commit -qm "Notes, fact chunk, map_metadata, filter errors" && echo ok"}

#!/bin/sh
# Build the ffmpeg-compatible tool from source (plain C, no external dependencies).
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
CC=${CC:-gcc}
# -ffp-contract=off keeps floating point evaluation strictly IEEE (no fused
# multiply-add), which the bit-exact FLAC analysis relies on.
$CC -O2 -std=gnu11 -ffp-contract=off -fno-fast-math -Wall -Wno-unused-function -Wno-unused-variable \
    -o executable src/*.c -lm
FINAL_OK
